description: A broad extraction of a macOS acquisition (an Expert Witness, sparse, VMDK or UDIF image, a raw APFS container or HFS+ volume, a raw disk with an Apple GPT partition, or a folder that is the root of a macOS volume): the pinned mac_apt 1.33.2 runs a plugin set over it in the input mode the object shows (FAST unless the target names its plugins) and writes its database, CSV files and log under mac_apt/. mac_apt exits 0 after errors it has logged, so the run reads its own log for one outcome per plugin (plugins.tsv: parsed, empty, unsupported or failed) and says complete only when mac_apt exited 0, the log has its start line and its finish line, every plugin the target names is parsed or empty and no error line or traceback sits outside a plugin; FAST and ALL can never be complete because the plugins they expand to are not listed by anything read here. mac_apt was never installed or run to build this recipe: its argument shape and the texts of the start, plugin start, plugin end, plugin exception and finish log lines were read from its v1.33.2 source (GitHub, 2026-11-04); the prefix of a log line, the wording of an empty or unsupported plugin and the per-plugin file names were not, and empty and unsupported rest on an assumed wording. Parsed rests on a log format never observed: a plugin is parsed when no line of its run holds an error word, and the source sets the log file format '%(asctime)s|%(name)s|%(levelname)s|%(message)s', read through a page summary and never seen in a real run, so that a failure logged below ERROR level or without an error word (permission denied, timed out, no such file, refused, skipping, errno) can still read as parsed and the run can then be complete. coverage.json is written first (partial) and replaced whole at the end; a run never writes over an earlier run. On arm64, where mac_apt is not installed (its statx helper stops at import), detect exits 1 with the packaging reason. The output is the examined system's own content: coverage.json marks every file it wrote under secret_bearing. ABANDONED CHILD: when mac_apt has ended, every process new in the recipe's own process group since it started is killed and waited for to be gone before any size, hash or log is read; if there was one the run is `partial` (plugins.program_group.left_behind in coverage.json). After that the files of the run are measured again one second later and, on Linux, the processes that hold one of them open are looked for: a file that grew or a holder makes the answer `partial` and the status basis says so. A process that started a session of its own (setsid) is not in the group and CANNOT be ended by this recipe; where its file did not grow within that second and it holds no file open, it is not seen and the files may still be growing. Where the recipe does not lead its process group, or the process table cannot be read, a note says what was not searched for. The log read is charged to the recipe's clock (what is left of --max-seconds, at least 10 seconds, never past 14250 seconds from the start, at most 512 MiB); a cut read, a line over 1 MiB, a line that holds a start, plugin or finish text without the line shape time|logger|LEVEL|message (a format read from the source and never observed: a message must begin with the text; a different real format reads as failed or partial, never as a wrong complete) and an error word or traceback in the last 65536 bytes of mac_apt.stdout or mac_apt.stderr each make the run `partial`.
object: macOS disk image, volume or mounted folder
exclusions: what no plugin of the pinned mac_apt release parses: those files stay in the source, unread by this extraction
deleted records beyond what a plugin reads itself (SQLite free pages, WAL): nothing is carved
an encrypted volume: no password is passed here, and what mac_apt does without one was never observed (the tool macos_triage takes a sealed password file)
UAC, Velociraptor and AFF4 inputs: this recipe does not detect them (the tool macos_triage takes them with an input type the caller names)
the plugins a FAST or ALL set expands to are not listed by anything read here, so a plugin that never started cannot be told from one that was not meant to
a plugin the log does not account for as parsed or empty: see plugins.tsv
covers: What mac_apt's plugins parse from the acquisition: its database, the per-plugin files of the CSV format and its log, kept whole under mac_apt/, with plugins.tsv holding the outcome of each plugin the log names or the target asked for. A plugin that finds nothing is empty only by an assumed wording of its log lines, a plugin that does not take the operating-system version is unsupported only by an assumed wording, and parsed is not a count of records and rests on a log format never observed (a failure logged below ERROR level or without an error word, such as permission denied, timed out, no such file, refused, skipping or errno, can still read as parsed); a plugin that failed, whose end the log does not show, or that never started is not covered, however many others wrote. The program runs in the recipe's own process group with a time limit of its own (--max-seconds, default 14100 seconds, under the 14400 of the limit): one that does not finish is ended with everything it started, what it wrote is kept, and the run says partial or failed, never complete; a stop signal ends the program and its children before the recipe ends. A run never writes over an earlier run's output. The output is the examined system's own content (a sensitive output).
